title: How to find HVAC businesses for roll-up research
summary: Build an HVAC research list by region, service mix, and ownership for a focused roll-up thesis.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


Start HVAC roll-up research with a defined service area and operating profile. Business data can help you find companies to investigate, while ownership checks and further conversations establish which businesses fit your sourcing criteria.


- Translate the sourcing thesis into observable geography and service criteria.
- Verify ownership and deduplicate branches before counting target companies.
- Keep financial fit and seller interest open until supported by evidence.


A list of HVAC contractors is an initial research universe. Turning it into an acquisition research list requires checking service mix, geography, ownership, and the evidence behind each record.


Public business data can help a sourcing team decide which companies deserve further investigation. It does not establish that an owner wants to sell or that a business meets financial underwriting requirements.


## 1. Translate the thesis into observable criteria


Start with the operating characteristics your team needs: service area, residential versus commercial work, maintenance offerings, installation work, and any required licenses.


For an example research brief, consider residential HVAC businesses serving a defined group of counties that publicly offer maintenance plans. Keep independent ownership as a verification requirement. A maintenance-plan page indicates an offering; it does not disclose recurring revenue.


Separate public screening criteria from questions requiring a conversation or documents. Revenue, EBITDA, customer concentration, and willingness to sell belong in the latter group unless supported by reliable evidence.


## 2. Assemble the initial business universe


Use category and location searches in[Openmart’s business database](https://www.openmart.com/products/local-business-database) , alongside contractor directories and company websites. Openmart also has a[private equity research solution](https://www.openmart.com/industry/private-equity) .


Keep the business name, website, location, source, and research date. Deduplicate branches and alternate trading names before counting companies. A location count and a company count answer different questions.


## 3. Check service mix and ownership


Read service pages and geographic coverage pages. Record what the company says it does rather than inferring service mix from its category alone.


Check acquisition announcements, company disclosures, and relevant public records for ownership context. When evidence conflicts or remains incomplete, flag the record for follow-up. Do not describe a company as independent solely because it uses a local brand name.


## 4. Use an evidence-based screening sheet


- **Service area:** Record publicly stated coverage
- **Service mix:** Link to relevant company pages
- **Maintenance offering:** Record the offering, not assumed revenue
- **Ownership:** Confirmed, unclear, or excluded, with source
- **Financial fit:** Unknown until supported
- **Seller interest:** Unknown until discussed
- **Next action:** Verify, contact, monitor, or exclude


Review websites and contact routes before a sourcing conversation. A business’s age, review count, or owner biography does not establish succession plans.


## 5. Validate before expanding the list


Start with 30 businesses in a focused region. Measure how many survive ownership checks, match the service thesis, and have a current business contact route. Record why others are excluded so the next search improves.


An exploratory introduction should accurately state who you are and the kind of business you want to learn about. Keep seller interest open until the owner expresses it.


Begin with[Openmart’s private equity solution](https://www.openmart.com/industry/private-equity) to explore business research. Use the resulting list to guide further verification and conversations; financial diligence remains a separate step.


## 6. Use portfolio evidence before labeling a local brand independent


TurnPoint’s[official brands directory](https://www.turnpointservices.com/turnpoint-brands/) lists 4 Seasons Heating & Air in Alpharetta and Cool Air Mechanical in Marietta among its local service brands. These examples show why a distinct local name or domain cannot settle an ownership question. For an independent-only sourcing brief, send such records to a platform-affiliation review before adding them to the independent target count. This is a public-record research example, not a statement about seller interest or acquisition availability.


- Brand: 4 Seasons Heating & Air.
- Public evidence: listed in TurnPoint’s official brands directory.
- Research decision: flag the documented platform relationship.
- Still to confirm: the current legal entity and whether it fits your investment mandate.


Record the portfolio source, the local company domain, and the date checked. Resolve contradictory evidence before outreach. Keep uncertain records in a separate review queue instead of treating absence from one portfolio as proof of independence.[The HVAC ownership checklist](https://www.openmart.com/blogs/verify-hvac-business-ownership-acquisition-research) provides the next steps.


Track distinct companies reviewed, companies passing the ownership screen, companies matching the service thesis, and owners agreeing to a sourcing conversation. Revenue estimates belong in an initial screening field. Use[the HVAC revenue data guide](https://www.openmart.com/blogs/hvac-company-owners-by-revenue-best-smb-data-sources-2026) to understand data-source choices; financial underwriting requires supporting financial information.


## Recommendation


Build an initial list of 30 businesses in one region. Use Openmart and company websites to research the service mix and footprint, then review ownership evidence. Track the reasons for including or excluding each company so your next search follows a more precise thesis.


[Start this research in Openmart](https://app.openmart.com/register?utm_source=openmart_blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=tam_pilot&utm_content=independent-hvac-business-list-roll-up-research) .


## FAQs


**Can public business data establish acquisition fit?**


It can support initial research. Financial statements, operating information, and a conversation with the owner are needed to evaluate the opportunity further.


**Does a local brand name prove independent ownership?**


No. An acquired business may retain its name. Check ownership disclosures and acquisition announcements before labeling it independent.


**Does offering a maintenance plan prove recurring revenue?**


The website establishes that the service is offered. The revenue mix and contract quality require supporting documents.
